title: A new viewer never waits behind a helper
description: Helper jobs (JS-024) may fill every free transcode slot but one across the cluster and hold it until their chunk is done, so a second viewer who starts at the same moment queues behind them. A viewer's job takes a helper's slot instead: the helper stops, and its chunk falls back to the job that asked for help (or to another helper later). Operators can turn helpers off.
acceptanceCriteria: With every slot but one held by helpers, two new viewers start at the same moment on separate worker processes and both get their first segment as fast as with no helpers running
The preempted helper's chunk is still made: the helped viewer plays through it with no stall beyond what a seek costs
A helper is never preempted by another helper
An operator setting turns helpers off; with it off, a slow job is one ffmpeg and inserts no helper rows; documented in docs/running.md
No preemption ever stops a viewer's own job
source: JS-024 post-task review (2026-11-08); the user chose to land JS-024 and fix this next
notes: Found reading the helper slot guard after the build: freeSlots is cluster-wide, so helpers keep one slot free for the whole cluster, not per worker. Priority 2 puts it ahead of JS-025. Built 2026-11-08: a viewer's job, under the cluster-wide helpers lock, cancels one helper when no slot is free (a queued one first, else the one furthest ahead, only on a live worker), then sends a preempt hint after its transaction commits; a running helper beats on that hint, and once as it subscribes, so it gives its slot back at once rather than at its next heartbeat. Measured: with a paused helper, a 10 s heartbeat and the viewer arriving just after the helper beat, the viewer's first segment took 5.75 s, the same as on an idle cluster; without the hint it was refused. transcodeHelpers: false on a worker turns its helpers off. Backlog: every viewer's ensure takes the cluster-wide helpers lock; transcodeHelpers is per worker, so mixed settings are possible; no check drives the config key through to the worker; a helper preempted during its pre-ffmpeg setup (subtitle extraction, fonts) sees the cancel only after ffmpeg starts; when queued viewers already exceed the free slots, a new viewer still cancels a helper whose slot goes to an earlier viewer; the preempt hint names no job, so every running helper beats once per preemption; operators see preemption only in the job's error and the log.
